chunks: And by his chain, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When you belch, do not raise (the sound of) your belching.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette regarding belching?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this instruction from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to highlight that even natural bodily functions should be performed with *adab* (etiquette) to avoid disturbing others, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on refining character (*akhlaq*) alongside worship. This specific guidance on belching serves as a practical application of modesty in public and private spheres, linking physical habits to spiritual refinement.

en.hubeali:
And by his chain, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When you belch, so do not raise (the loudness of) you belching’.
en.sarwar: 6. Through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith the following is narrated: ‘Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘When you belch then do not make it loud.’”
